subject: Payments provider — subprocessor inventory & crypto residency clarifications
messages:
From: Claire Mercer <claire@bluewavepay.com>

Cc: payments-security@bluewavepay.com, BlueWave Pay Procurement <procurement@bluewavepay.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: PSP subprocessor inventory + crypto residency

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the demo last week — the integration looks promising. Procurement asked us to collect a few items before we can move to legal review. Can you share: 

- A current subprocessor / vendor roster (names + roles + country of processing)
- SOC 2 Type II summary (we don't need the full report yet)
- Confirmation of where any payment-related encryption keys are stored (KMS region / provider)

We are particularly picky about key residency for PSP integrations (financial data), so any short diagram or note about key management would help speed review. Target timeline from our side: we need this by EOD Tuesday (your timezone) to hit our procurement window.

If you prefer I can send a formal questionnaire (SIG-lite) — happy either way.

Thanks,
Claire Mercer
Senior Security Analyst
BlueWave Pay

Subject: Re: Request: PSP subprocessor inventory + crypto residency

Hi Claire — looping in a couple of clarifying points from our security team to make procurement's job easier. Quick answers followed by asks: 

1) Key custody and residency
- For hosted customers: by default we manage application-level encryption keys (envelope keys) in provider-managed KMS in the same cloud region as the active deployment. For payment token material we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in customer KMS projects; those are bound to customer-managed projects/accounts and *do not* exit those KMS scopes.
- For Dedicated / Private deployments: keys are controlled by the customer KMS/HSM; Redwood operates with key references only.

2) Access controls and logging
- Access to key material requires approval and is logged (KMS audit logs + Redwood operator audit). We can provide a redacted log sample for a short window on request.

3) Subprocessor specifics you might care about
- Payment routing partners (listed in the CSV) are contractually limited to processing transaction metadata only; tokenization and cardholder data are processed in our PCI-compliant enclave.

Actions we need from BlueWave so we can finalize an attestation: 
- Confirm whether you require keys to be customer-managed (CMK) or if provider-managed keys in the US-east region meet your policy.
- If you require a SIG-lite questionnaire, please attach it (or a template). Otherwise we will prepare a short CAIQ extract and a vendor attestation page.

We can have a vendor attestation letter back to you by EOD Wednesday (Redwood time) if you confirm the key residency requirement today.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Neha / Nikhil —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. BlueWave's requirement: customer-managed keys (CMK) in a US jurisdiction is preferred for card-token material. That said, if you can provide a vendor attestation stating how the CMK integration works (reference architecture + service account separation + audit log sample) we can accept provider-coordinated CMK where the customer retains administrative control.

Next steps from BlueWave: procurement will review the CSV and SOC summary today. We will upload a SIG-lite questionnaire if we need granular mapping; at this point procurement asked for the attestation and the KMS diagram (your dataflow). Delivery timeline: procurement expects the attestation by Thursday COB our time (Thursday 2027-03-11 23:59 PST).

If you can confirm you'll deliver the attestation + CAIQ extract by Thu COB, we'll mark this satisfied and move to legal. Also please include any relevant DocuSign or procurement reference when you send the attestation.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Claire Mercer

BlueWave Pay
